summary.title: Monthly payroll by employee
summary.formula: Net pay = salary + bonuses and accruals − penalties and deductions − advances. Only approved and paid entries count.
summary.ownEmptyHint: It appears once your account is linked to an employee record.
summary.emptyHint: Lists current employees and everyone with entries for the month.

salary.title: Monthly salary
salary.invalid: Enter the salary as a number of zero or more

payroll.title: Payroll
payroll.introOwn: Your accruals and deductions by month. Drafts are hidden until they are approved.
payroll.intro: Entries are added by hand; later the attendance system will be able to create them too.
payroll.emptyBody: An advance, bonus, penalty or deduction enters the month’s payroll once it is approved.
payroll.deleteDetail: Only a draft or cancelled entry can be deleted; it is not part of the month’s payroll.

overview.heading: Financial overview
overview.intro: A cash view of the period: inflow is payments received, expenses are expenses recorded. Receivables and overdue amounts are as of today. Amounts in different currencies are never added together.
overview.emptyPeriod: No payments, expenses or open invoices for {period}.
overview.cashflowHint: The month’s net is shown under each pair. Hover over a bar to see the amount.
overview.categoriesHint: Total {total}. A category opens the list of its expenses.
overview.categoriesEmpty: No expenses in {currency} for the period.
overview.projectsHint: Cumulative to {date}: actual = expenses + hours paid at rate, margin = inflow − actual. Worst margin first.
overview.projectsEmpty: No active projects with a budget or money movement.
overview.upcomingTitle: Due in the next {n} day | Due in the next {n} days
overview.upcomingEmpty: Nothing falls due in the coming days.
overview.payrollHint: Approved and paid entries are counted. Payroll is not part of the expenses above until it is recorded as a “{category}” expense.
overview.payrollEmpty: No salaries or entries for the month.

cashflow.empty: No money moved in {currency} during the period.

budgetLines.title: Budget by category
budgetLines.otherCurrencies: There are expenses in {currencies} — they are not part of the actual for this {currency} budget.
budgetLines.mismatch: The category total {lines} does not match the budget’s planned cost {planned}.
budgetLines.actualHint: Actual is the project’s expenses in the category; timesheet labour is not part of the breakdown.

expenses.emptyBody: A project expense counts towards its actual cost; an expense without a project goes to studio overheads.
expenses.deleteDetail: The record disappears from the lists and from the project’s actual cost.

payments.periodHint: A paid payment belongs to its payment date, an expected one to its due date.
payments.emptyBody: A payment belongs to a client and can settle an invoice issued to them.
payments.deleteDetail: The payment disappears from the lists and no longer counts towards paying the invoice.

cover.title: Invoice covered
cover.message: Invoice {number} for {amount} is fully covered by payments. Mark it as paid?
cover.detail: The invoice status changes only through this confirmation — the payment itself never touches it.
cover.failed: Couldn’t mark the invoice as paid

invoices.emptyBody: An invoice is issued to a client and settled by the payments against it.
invoices.deleteDetail: The invoice disappears from the lists. Its payments stay but lose the link to it.

budgets.intro: Each project’s plan next to its actual. The actual is never typed in: it is the project’s expenses plus hours paid at rate, in the budget currency. The category breakdown is behind the button in each row; the summary across all projects is in the {link}.
budgets.emptyBody: A budget sets a project’s planned revenue and cost — margin and burn are measured against them.
budgets.deleteDetail: The planned figures and the category breakdown will be removed, and the project will be measured against the budget on its card.

financial.intro: Invoiced, received and spent by month, the expense breakdown, and receivables by age of debt.
financial.mixedCurrencies: The selection holds several currencies ({currencies}). The totals below add them up as one — narrow the period or separate the currencies before relying on these amounts.
financial.monthsEmpty: No money moved in the selected period.
financial.ageingHint: Unpaid invoices as of today — the report period does not affect this table.

clients.title: Clients report
clients.heading: Clients
clients.intro: How much each client was invoiced, how much came in and what is left. The report works from invoices: a payment not linked to an invoice does not appear here — that money shows in the financial report. Average time to pay counts closed invoices only.
clients.empty: Nothing was invoiced to clients in the selected period.
clients.mixedCurrencies: Clients are billed in different currencies. The totals below add them up as one — read the rows, not the sum.

time.title: Time report
time.heading: Time and people
time.intro: Hours logged per employee, valued at their rate. Hours without a rate are counted but cost nothing — they have a column of their own.
time.empty: Nobody logged hours in the selected period.
time.unpricedWarning: {hours} h were logged by people without a rate — those hours are not in the cost. The total below is understated by exactly them.

production.title: Production report
production.heading: Production
production.intro: The state of live projects: progress, missed deadlines and open revisions. Cancelled and archived projects are left out.
production.empty: No live projects — the report has nothing to show.
